$comment: Identity is frozen by artifacts/design/rule-catalog-v1.md. Both rules are scoped by the viewport classes the project's policy declares — a project that declares only desktop is not judged against a phone it never claimed to support (Standard 28).

rules.title: Behavior at each declared viewport class is defined
rules.description: For every viewport class the project declares support for, the intended layout and interaction behavior is defined — including what is deliberately degraded or omitted there.
rules.rationale: Undefined responsive behavior is not absent behavior; it is whatever the layout happens to do, discovered by users on the devices nobody tested.
rules.remediation: Define behavior per declared viewport class, and record deliberate degradation as a decision rather than leaving it as an artifact.
rules.$assuranceNote: The presence of a definition per declared class is checkable. Whether the implementation matches it needs rendering at those viewports.

rules.title: Content does not overflow unintentionally
rules.description: At every declared viewport class, content stays within its container unless the overflow is a designed, scrollable affordance.
rules.rationale: Horizontal overflow hides content behind an edge with no indication that anything is there, and it is the most common way a layout fails on a real device.
rules.remediation: Let the container constrain the content, or make the overflow an explicit scroll region.
rules.$assuranceNote: Overflow is a property of resolved layout with real content at a real width. It is established only for viewports and routes a run exercised.
